title: How to use Magic Move in Keynote on Mac: step by step guide
metaTitle: How to use Magic Move in Keynote on Mac: Step-by-Step
description: Learn how to use Magic Move in Keynote on Mac to create cinematic transitions. Follow our clear, step-by-step instructions to master this powerful effect.
targetKeyword: how to use magic move in keynote on mac
intro: To use Magic Move in Keynote on Mac, you must duplicate a slide and then modify the objects on the second slide. This allows Keynote to track the movement, resizing, or rotation of those objects when you apply the transition effect.
tldr: Duplicate your starting slide using Command + D.
Move or resize objects on the second slide.
Select the first slide in the pair.
Open the Animate sidebar and select Magic Move.
Click Preview to test your animation.

blocks.text: Magic Move is a transition effect that automatically animates objects between two slides. It works by matching objects that exist on both slides. If you move an object on the second slide, Keynote calculates the path and animates it during the transition. It replaces the need for manual keyframing or complex motion paths.

The key to success is keeping objects consistent. If you delete an object and create a new one, the animation will fail. You must duplicate your slide to ensure the internal IDs match. This process is essential for creating professional, cinematic transitions.
How to Use Magic Move in Keynote on Mac
Follow these steps to set up your first Magic Move transition. Ensure you are using the latest version of Keynote on macOS 26.

Many users report that objects dissolve rather than move. This usually happens when Keynote cannot identify the objects as the same. Avoid copying and pasting objects between slides. Always use the duplicate function.

If text animation feels jittery, the engine might be struggling to match individual characters. A known workaround is to add a hidden character like a semicolon with zero percent opacity at the end of the text on both slides. This helps the tracking engine maintain consistency.

While Magic Move is powerful, it is easy to overuse. Experts recommend applying it to only 30 to 40 percent of your transitions. Too much animation can distract your audience from your content. Use it to emphasize key changes or to guide the eye through a complex diagram.

Remember that the Mac app offers the full suite of animation tools. While Keynote for iCloud is convenient, it may not render complex animations exactly as you see them on your Mac. Always preview your presentation on the device you plan to use for the actual talk.

faq.question: Why does my object dissolve instead of moving?
faq.answer: This happens when Keynote cannot match the object between slides. Always duplicate your slide rather than copying and pasting objects to ensure they keep the same internal ID.

faq.question: Can I use Magic Move in the web version of Keynote?
faq.answer: While Keynote for iCloud supports basic editing, it lacks the full animation engine found in the macOS app. Complex Magic Move transitions may not render correctly.

faq.question: How do I fix jittery text animations?
faq.answer: Text animation issues often occur when Keynote cannot track individual characters. Adding a hidden character like a semicolon with zero percent opacity at the end of the text on both slides can help.

task: How to use Magic Move in Keynote on Mac
requirements: A presentation with at least two slides

steps.name: Prepare your slides
steps.text: Create your first slide and add the objects you want to animate. Make sure these objects are placed exactly where you want them to start.

steps.name: Duplicate the slide
steps.text: In the slide navigator on the left, select your slide and press Command + D. This ensures the internal object IDs are preserved for the transition.

steps.name: Modify the second slide
steps.text: On the new slide, move, resize, or rotate your objects to their desired end position. Do not delete and recreate them.

steps.name: Apply Magic Move
steps.text: Select the first slide in your pair. Open the Animate sidebar on the right, click Add an Effect, and choose Magic Move from the menu.

steps.name: Preview the animation
steps.text: Click the Preview button in the Animate sidebar to see how your objects move between the slides. Adjust the duration slider as needed.

troubleshooting.problem: Objects are dissolving instead of moving
troubleshooting.fix: Ensure you are duplicating the slide rather than copying and pasting objects between separate slides.
Add a hidden character like a semicolon with 0 percent opacity at the end of the text on both slides.

lazur.spoken: Where is the Magic Move button?
lazur.result: Lazur circles the Add an Effect button in the Animate sidebar.
